text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [AUTO-PAGE] p99 latency spike & 5xx surge on prod-route /v1/generate (svc:model-serving-prod). Alert threshold breached at 2026-03-14T21:45Z. Auto-escalation to SRE oncall.

sre-naomi: I'm oncall, looking. Paging querytrace, grabbing recent deploys. Anyone touching kernel flags or batching config in the last 20m?

eng-eli: I deployed canary rev=rev-2026-03-14-8a1 on the cluster 20m ago. No feature flags, just a small lib compile with new attention kernel. Rolling only on canary.

oncall-zoe: Naomi / Eli, can we confirm if canary is in prod pool? Graph shows p99 jump coincident with canary rollout.

sre-naomi: checking canary host list now. I see 12% of traffic routed to canary via routing rule. QPS steady but error rate up. Running quick top across pods.

sre-naomi: logs:
```
[2026-03-14T21:45:12Z] WARN request timeout route=/v1/generate latency=6000ms host=svc-gn-08
[2026-03-14T21:45:13Z] ERROR downstream 502 gateway timeout kvcache miss=true
[2026-03-14T21:45:14Z] WARN request stall seq_len=2048 model=gpt-open-8b
```

eng-eli: those hosts are exactly the canary ones. The new kernel has an aggressive KV prefetch; could be starving I/O under certain seq_len distributions. Happened once in staging but we didn't see p99 like this.

support-raj: Support queue seeing a spike. ~40 tickets in the last 15m; some customers reporting generation timeouts. No data exfil.

pm-maya: Any ETA on mitigation? Customers asking for status update.

oncall-zoe: Naomi, if canary is the culprit we should revert canary or shift traffic. Do we have permission to cut traffic to canary immediately?

sre-naomi: I can reroute at the load balancer. Two options: 1) remove canary from pool (instant), or 2) rollback deployment (requires CI approval but faster to remove canary). I'd prefer remove canary from LB first to stop impact while we decide.

eng-eli: I'm preparing a rollback patch. If you can drain canary while I trigger rollback that buys time.

sre-naomi: Doing immediate route shift now. Command:
```
# remove canary tag from prod route
redwoodctl routes update --route /v1/generate --remove-tag canary-2026-03-14-8a1
```

sre-naomi: Done. Confirming traffic shift... backend mix now 100% stable nodes.

incident-bot: METRIC_CHANGE: p99 latency dropped from 5.1s -> 1.2s over 30s. 5xx rate reduced by 72%.

support-raj: Support update: initial reports decreasing. Telling customers we mitigated and investigating root cause. No commitment yet.

eng-eli: Initiating full rollback to rev-2026-03-13-zz9 now (CI kick). I'll post status when rollback completed.

eng-eli: rollback CI success. Rollback started, pods terminating for canary and new pods from previous image launching.

sre-naomi: Monitoring. p95/p99 trending down. Still seeing a few tail timeouts from in-flight requests, but within SLO.

oncall-zoe: Thanks team. Naomi, continue to monitor for 30m. Eli, we'll coordinate a proper postmortem and decide whether to revert kernel change in branch.

pm-maya: Noting customer impact: estimated ~50 affected sessions, top impacted customers: acme-inc, shopfast. We'll prep a customer note.

sre-naomi: Handoff: I'm on for the next 30m then handing to oncall-zoe for evening. Postmortem assignee: eng-eli (root cause), sre-naomi (mitigation timeline), pm-maya (customer comms).

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) - Duration 00:28:47. Create postmortem link: <https://redwood.internal/incidents/6278901234>

oncall-zoe: Adding a quick checklist to the incident doc: reproduce with long sequences, run KV prefetch stress, add canary traffic cap to 5% next time.

support-raj: Sending interim customer note: "We've mitigated the spike by rolling back a deploy. We're investigating root cause; will share findings." :thumbsup: 

eng-eli: Adding an immediate action: revert kernel change, run full load tests with seq_len=2048+, and update canary gating to include p99 smoke.

sre-naomi: Thanks all. I'll follow up with a brief telemetry dump and link to logs in the incident doc. Leaving channel, handing to oncall-zoe.

oncall-zoe: Acknowledged. I'll watch the metrics and escalate if it resurfaces. Good job team. :raised_hands:
